question: Which of the following inert gases is used to inflate party balloons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Helium is an inert gas
 
• Because of its inertness, it does not react with other substances. Hence Helium is used in balloons.
 
• Properties of Helium
 
 
• It has the lowest boiling point of any element at -2690C and a low density .
 
• This allows Helium to float.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• In the modern periodic table, group 18 belongs to inert gases.
 
• This group of a series of gases including Argon, Helium, Neon, Krypton, Xenon, and Radon.
 
• **Radon **is the only radioactive out of all and its also not present in the Atmosphere.
